page: Amazon Web Services i7i.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 1875 GB NVMe SSD, while networking baseline performance is rated at 5 Gbps. The server operates on the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7i.2xlarge demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. It achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as Gzip and Bzip3, show strong performance in the top 25%, alongside a strong Passmark memory score. Multi-core performance, static web serving, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. However, the server exhibits a performance tradeoff in LLM inference for text generation using medium 7B models, where it registers in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.2xlarge offers a high-density storage and memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitative fit for workloads requiring fast local storage access without the overhead of larger compute instances. It is highly suited for database operations, transactional workloads, caching layers, and data-intensive applications that leverage its bundled NVMe SSD and DDR5 memory.
